sections.html:
Sandoval County is part of the Albuquerque metro area, with 148,834 residents in the 2020 census. Bernalillo is the county seat, and Rio Rancho is the other principal community. The county spans 3,716 square miles, so a sale here might be a suburban lot in Rio Rancho or a larger rural or mountain parcel elsewhere. Where the property sits decides which agencies show up on its tax bill.

Intel's Rio Rancho campus has shaped that market for decades, so sale timing for Rio Rancho owners can follow the local job market.

Billing and collection happen in Bernalillo, at 1500 Idalia Road, Building D, NM 87004. Doors are open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The Assessor handles valuation separately.

  • Phone: 505-867-7581 or toll free 1-800-332-8022
  • Email: treasurers@sandovalcountynm.gov
  • Mail: P.O. Box 40, Bernalillo, NM 87004
  • Closed for a staff meeting 2:30 to 3:30 p.m. on the third Wednesday of each month
  • Services and phone payments in English and Spanish
  • During tax season, appointments before 8 a.m. and after 5 p.m. on request at 505-867-7579

You can request a statement of taxes due at any time. Card payments carry a convenience fee, and allow 72 hours for a payment to post.

Education takes the largest share. The Treasurer's chart for tax year 2025 splits it this way:

  • Education: 42 percent
  • Municipal government: 21 percent
  • County government: 20 percent
  • State, conservancy and other: 13 percent
  • Contracting hospitals: 5 percent

County programs funded include fire and 911, libraries, public safety, senior programs, roads, the landfill and the detention center. What you personally owe depends on which school district, town and special taxing districts include your lot.

The year follows the statewide schedule, and the Treasurer's FAQ lists the dates that matter.

DateWhat happens
January 1Date of assessment; ownership and values are set as of this day
February 28Last day to report value changes, apply for exemptions or remove destroyed property
April 1Assessor mails the Notice of Value
October 1Tax roll goes from the Assessor to the Treasurer
November 1Tax bills mailed; the only bill the owner receives
November 10 to December 10First half due, without penalty through December 10
April 10 to May 10Second half due, without penalty through May 10
June 10Delinquent notices prepared and mailed
July 1Delinquency list for parcels over two years behind goes to the state

Late charges are 1 percent of the base tax per month in interest, plus 1 percent per month in penalty, with a penalty maximum of 5 percent and a minimum of $5. A returned check adds $25 or 5 percent of the check, whichever is greater.

Tell the Assessor about changes in writing. An address change must be signed by the owner on record with the Assessor, because bills go to the address on the Assessor's roll and may not be forwarded when you moved over half a year back.

A bill can fail to arrive because an address change came in after printing, a data entry error, or mail lost among the more than 100,000 bills the office sends. A bill can also rise because of a higher assessed value, a lost exemption, a different school district, a higher mil levy or a voter-approved bond.

A clean record speeds up a closing. Before listing or accepting an offer, confirm the owner of record, the mailing address and the status of both halves of the current year, then ask the Treasurer for a statement of taxes due.

Your protest clock starts the day the Notice of Value is mailed and lasts thirty days. The last day of that period is also the final date to claim a family or veteran exemption, to apply for agricultural valuation, to report improvements costing more than $10,000 or to submit a statement of decrease in value.

The petition needs your name and address, a description of the parcel, your reason, and the figure you think is right. The state's protest pamphlet has the details. A county board of three hears the case, owes you a decision inside 180 days, and can be challenged in district court within thirty days after that.

Residential increases are capped as well, at the higher of 103 percent of last year's value or 106.1 percent of the value two years back, unless it is a first-year valuation, a new improvement, or follows a sale.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill at a sale
sections.html:
Sandoval County has no proration service. The bill follows whoever is the owner on record, and it is mailed even when a lender escrows the payment. Seller and buyer divide the year themselves in the closing paperwork.

  • Sold after October 1? The bill that arrives still shows your name and address.
  • Buyers should send the Assessor a mailing address right after the County Clerk records the deed.
  • A mobile home cannot change title without a tax release, which is paid in certified funds and issued by appointment.
  • Tax liability exists even if a bill was never received, under Section 7-38-36 NMSA 1978.

The State of New Mexico and its counties do not run tax deed, tax certificate or tax lien sales. The only sales are state auctions for parcels with two or more years of delinquent tax. Cash Home Buyers works with Sandoval County owners who want to sell before that point, with no repairs and no commission.

sections.h2: Your closing timeline in Sandoval County
sections.html:
Sandoval County sales move fastest when the paperwork lines up early. Here is a sensible order.

  1. Call the Treasurer for a statement of taxes due, which covers both halves of the current year and anything older.
  2. Check with the Assessor that the owner of record and mailing address are right, and report any change in writing.
  3. Tell the title company about any protest or exemption on file so the closing statement matches the county record.
  4. Decide with the buyer how the year's tax is split, since the Treasurer does not do it for you.
  5. After closing, make sure the buyer gets a mailing address to the Assessor so the next November bill finds the right person.

A cash sale skips the lender's review, so the main limit on speed is how quickly the tax balance and title are cleared. Bring a copy of your deed, a photo ID and your latest tax bill to any meeting with the title company, and keep the Treasurer's statement of taxes due with your closing papers. If your property is a mobile home, book the tax release appointment early, because releases are scheduled rather than walk-in.

faqs.q: Where is the Sandoval County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: It is at 1500 Idalia Road, Building D, in Bernalillo, NM 87004, on the first floor. Call 505-867-7581 or 1-800-332-8022, or write to P.O. Box 40, Bernalillo, NM 87004.

faqs.q: When are Sandoval County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due November 10 and is paid without penalty through December 10. The second half is due April 10 and is paid without penalty through May 10.

faqs.q: What are the late fees on Sandoval County property tax?
faqs.a: Interest is 1 percent of the base tax per month. The penalty is also 1 percent per month, capped at 5 percent, with a $5 minimum.

faqs.q: Does the county prorate property tax when I sell?
faqs.a: No. The county offers no proration. Sellers and buyers split the year in their closing paperwork.

faqs.q: Can Sandoval County sell my house for unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Not the county itself. Only the state holds auctions, for parcels two or more years behind, and the Treasurer passes the delinquency list to the state on July 1.
